title: Detecting GitHound Enumeration via the GitHub API
content_md: For many organizations, GitHub Enterprise serves as a central platform for software development, collaboration, and source code management. This makes it an increasingly valuable target for attackers seeking access to source code, sensitive information, credentials, and development infrastructure. Recent incidents demonstrate an increasing preference among attackers for targeting GitHub environments. In March 2026, the Trivy supply-chain attack involved stolen credentials being used to publish malicious releases and tamper with GitHub Actions. The compromise subsequently extended to Checkmarx’s GitHub environment, where attackers gained unauthorized repository access and distributed malicious code through developer tools and CI/CD . In May 2026, GitHub itself disclosed that an employee device had been compromised through a malicious VS Code extension, resulting in the exfiltration of internal repositories . In May 2026, a reported exposure of sensitive CISA information through a public GitHub repository highlighted how misconfigured access and unintended data disclosure can expose sensitive information. These incidents highlight the growing importance of protecting and monitoring code repositories.
